evidence.name: Workshop Scene Evidence

actualProperties.bodyPosition: Grant is located near a ladder and work area in a position initially capable of suggesting an accidental fall.
actualProperties.bloodPattern: Blood distribution and impact characteristics are inconsistent with a single uncomplicated fall.
actualProperties.ladderCondition: The ladder is displaced but lacks a fully convincing physical relationship to the fatal injury pattern.
actualProperties.sceneDisturbance: Several nearby objects appear moved after the primary injury event.
actualProperties.toolEnvironment: Multiple construction tools are present, including a framing hammer consistent with the general class of object capable of producing the injuries.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: The observed scene is inconsistent with a simple accidental ladder fall. Physical findings support an assault followed by limited staging.
Blood distribution indicates more than one significant impact event and does not align with the apparent ladder-fall mechanism.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Establishes that the apparent accident is unreliable and supports classification of the death as an intentional assault.
contaminationRisks: Uncontrolled movement through the workshop may compromise trace interpretation.
Moving the ladder or tools before documentation may reduce reconstruction quality.
admissibilityRisks: Poor scene documentation may weaken expert conclusions.

evidence.name: Workshop Tool and Footwear Trace Package

actualProperties.framingHammer: A framing hammer from the workshop is consistent in general size, mass, and shape with the injury mechanism.
actualProperties.weaponDefinitiveness: The hammer cannot by itself conclusively identify who used it.
actualProperties.footwearTrace: A partial footwear impression is preserved near the meaningful assault area.
actualProperties.footwearSpecificity: The impression contains class characteristics useful for comparison but is not uniquely identifying.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: The framing hammer is physically compatible with the injury class but cannot be identified as the weapon to the exclusion of all similar tools.
The partial impression supports comparison against candidate footwear and may include or exclude certain tread patterns. It is corroborative rather than individually conclusive.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Provides a forensic route into method and possible scene-presence comparisons without becoming a single-source identification clue.
contaminationRisks: Footwear impressions are vulnerable to trampling.
Tool handling before collection may compromise trace evidence.
admissibilityRisks: Overstating a class-characteristic footwear comparison would create evidentiary weakness.

evidence.name: Grant Holloway Wearable Data

actualProperties.lastNormalActivity: Normal movement and physiological readings continue into the late evening.
actualProperties.criticalEventWindow: Abrupt abnormal readings occur approximately during the 10:14 PM to 10:18 PM window.
actualProperties.postEventActivity: No meaningful voluntary activity is recorded after the critical event.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: The data supports a critical physiological event occurring at approximately 10:16 PM, with a reasonable forensic window of several minutes.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Narrows the homicide window and permits comparison against suspect movements and alibis.
admissibilityRisks: The device time should be validated against network or phone time before investigators claim minute-level precision.

evidence.name: Grant Holloway Phone Extraction

actualProperties.accountantMessage: Grant indicates that he found something serious in the company records and wants to meet the following morning.
actualProperties.ashleyConversation: Grant and Ashley exchange messages later that evening. The surviving portions become increasingly tense.
actualProperties.deletionArtifacts: Technical artifacts indicate that portions of the Ashley conversation were removed after the homicide.
actualProperties.exactDeletedTextAvailability: Not every deleted message is fully recoverable.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: Extraction confirms Grant's 9:36 PM communication with the accountant and the later exchange with Ashley.
Metadata and recoverable fragments establish that portions of the Grant-Ashley conversation were deleted after the homicide. The recovery does not reconstruct every deleted sentence.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Links Grant's financial discovery to Ashley, establishes pre-homicide contact, and provides evidence of post-event concealment.
admissibilityRisks: Recovered fragments must not be represented as complete messages when only metadata or partial text survives.

evidence.name: Nora Bell Witness Observation Record

actualProperties.vehicleObservation: Nora observed a dark SUV near Grant's property during the relevant period.
actualProperties.colorMemory: Nora initially recalls the SUV as black.
actualProperties.canonicalVehicleColor: Ashley's SUV is very dark blue.
actualProperties.lightingConditions: Nighttime lighting reasonably explains the color discrepancy.
actualProperties.timingPrecision: Nora's times are approximate until anchored by other records.
actualProperties.voiceObservation: Nora heard raised voices but cannot reliably identify the speakers.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Provides independent corroboration of vehicle activity while demonstrating that eyewitness recollection can be useful without being perfect.
contaminationRisks: Suggestive questioning could distort later identification or confidence.
admissibilityRisks: Investigators should preserve Nora's original uncertainty and avoid converting an approximate observation into false certainty.

evidence.name: Hollis and Holloway Vendor Records

actualProperties.paymentPattern: Repeated payments exist that initially resemble ordinary vendor expenses.
actualProperties.supportingDocuments: Expected invoices, delivery records, contact history, and ordinary vendor documentation are incomplete or absent.
actualProperties.businessExistence: Investigation fails to locate a normal operating vendor corresponding to the payment pattern.
actualProperties.totalLoss: The amount is substantial enough to create a serious motive but is not necessary to prove the homicide by itself.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: Northline Fixtures demonstrates characteristics inconsistent with an ordinary active supplier and consistent with a fictitious vendor payment scheme.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Establishes the underlying financial fraud and supplies a credible motive for preventing Grant from exposing it.
admissibilityRisks: Financial conclusions should be supported by authenticated records rather than investigator summaries alone.

evidence.name: Vendor System Access Metadata

actualProperties.accountAssociation: Activity involving Northline Fixtures is associated with credentials and workstation access assigned to Ashley.
actualProperties.legitimateAccessContext: Ashley legitimately uses the same systems as part of her employment.
actualProperties.suspiciousActivity: The timing and pattern of access overlap with creation, maintenance, or approval activity for Northline Fixtures.
actualProperties.individualProofLimit: Credentials alone do not independently prove that Ashley personally performed every recorded action.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: System logs materially connect Ashley's assigned credentials or workstation activity to suspicious Northline Fixtures activity. The result requires corroboration because Ashley had legitimate access to the system.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Connects Ashley to the fraud while preserving enough ambiguity that the player must corroborate motive with additional evidence.
admissibilityRisks: Investigators must not characterize shared or legitimate-access metadata as exclusive identification without support.

evidence.name: Ashley Williams Movement Record

actualProperties.vehicleDescription: Ashley drives a very dark blue SUV.
actualProperties.movementPattern: Available records place Ashley or her vehicle in the area of Grant's residence during the relevant period.
actualProperties.arrivalSupport: The evidence is consistent with arrival shortly after 10:00 PM.
actualProperties.departureSupport: The evidence is consistent with departure shortly after the homicide window.
actualProperties.precisionLimit: No single location record places Ashley at an exact square-foot position inside the workshop.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: Combined movement information materially supports Ashley's presence near Grant's residence during the homicide window and conflicts with a categorical denial that she went there.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Provides opportunity evidence and corroborates Nora's imperfect observation.
admissibilityRisks: Location precision must not be overstated.
Records acquired without appropriate legal authority may become unusable.

evidence.name: Ashley Williams SUV Trace Evidence

actualProperties.searchRequirement: The relevant areas of the vehicle require valid consent or other lawful search authority.
actualProperties.cleaningIndicators: The cargo area shows signs of recent cleaning inconsistent with ordinary accumulated dirt patterns.
actualProperties.presumptiveFinding: A small cleaned or partially cleaned stain reacts consistently with possible blood.
actualProperties.canonicalSource: The biological material originates from Grant Holloway.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: A concealed or partially cleaned area in the SUV produces a presumptive positive indication for blood.
The recovered biological profile is consistent with Grant Holloway and provides strong physical corroboration connecting Grant's blood to Ashley's vehicle.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: One of the strongest physical corroboration items in the case. It substantially strengthens the homicide theory but remains dependent on lawful collection and admissibility.
contaminationRisks: Failure to use clean collection procedures may create contamination arguments.
admissibilityRisks: An unlawful vehicle search may result in suppression.
Exceeding the authorized search scope may jeopardize collection.
Weak chain-of-custody documentation may reduce evidentiary weight.

evidence.name: Grant Holloway Laptop

actualProperties.canonicalPossession: The laptop is located within Ashley's control during a properly authorized search.
actualProperties.financialMaterial: The laptop contains Grant's working notes and copies of financial records relating to Northline Fixtures.
actualProperties.recentActivity: Recent documents demonstrate that Grant was actively examining the suspicious transactions shortly before his death.

canonicalForensicResults.resultData: The device is confirmed as Grant's missing laptop. Recent files demonstrate his ongoing Northline Fixtures investigation.
A forensic image preserves Grant's recent financial analysis and supporting files without requiring investigators to work directly from the original device.

evidence.canonicalSignificance: Strongly corroborates Ashley's concealment behavior, links the homicide to the financial motive, and demonstrates possession of property removed from the crime scene.
contaminationRisks: Opening or altering files before forensic imaging may change metadata.
admissibilityRisks: Recovery outside valid warrant scope may result in suppression.
A separate or sufficiently broad digital-search authorization may be required to examine device contents.
Failure to preserve a forensic image may create authenticity challenges.
